files.README.md:
# shopflow_dbt -- capstone reference solution (Chapter 26)

This repository is the reference solution of the ShopFlow capstone project of
*The dbt Analytics Engineering Bible*. Each milestone of Chapter 26 is one commit
with an annotated tag: `m00`, `m01`, ... `m14`.

## Layout expected on your machine
```
~/dbt-course/
  shopflow-data/      # copy of labs/capstone (data/, setup.sql, updates/) + shopflow.duckdb
  shopflow_dbt/       # this dbt project (your own repo)
```
Build the raw database once: `cd ~/dbt-course/shopflow-data && duckdb shopflow.duckdb < setup.sql`.

## Use the tags to compare with your work
```bash
git tag -n                      # list milestones with their message
git diff m03 m04 --stat         # what changed in one milestone
git checkout m04                # look at the solution of milestone 4 (read-only visit)
git switch main                 # come back
```
Copy `profiles.example.yml` into `~/.dbt/profiles.yml` (profile name `shopflow`).
Always run dbt from this folder (the database path is relative).
files.dbt_project.yml:
name: 'shopflow_dbt'
version: '1.0.0'

# the profile (connection) defined in ~/.dbt/profiles.yml
profile: 'shopflow'

model-paths: ["models"]
analysis-paths: ["analyses"]
test-paths: ["tests"]
seed-paths: ["seeds"]
macro-paths: ["macros"]
snapshot-paths: ["snapshots"]

clean-targets:
  - "target"
  - "dbt_packages"

vars:
  revenue_start_date: '2025-07-01'
  revenue_end_date: '2026-01-03'      # exclusive: the spine stops on 2026-01-02

models:
  shopflow_dbt:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
      +schema: staging
    intermediate:
      +materialized: view
      +schema: intermediate
    marts:
      +materialized: table
      finance:
        +schema: finance
      marketing:
        +schema: marketing

seeds:
  shopflow_dbt:
    +schema: seeds

files.models/intermediate/_int__unit_tests.yml:
unit_tests:
  - name: test_eur_conversion_uses_the_rate_of_the_order_month
    description: >
      An order is converted to EUR with the rate of ITS month and currency.
      Net amount = paid - refunded, converted with the same rate.
    model: int_orders__enriched
    given:
      - input: ref('stg_shopflow_app__orders')
        rows:
          - {order_id: 1, customer_id: 10, order_at: 2025-07-15 10:00:00, order_date: 2025-07-15, order_status: delivered, currency_code: MAD, updated_at: 2025-07-20 08:00:00}
          - {order_id: 2, customer_id: 11, order_at: 2025-12-03 09:30:00, order_date: 2025-12-03, order_status: returned, currency_code: USD, updated_at: 2025-12-12 08:00:00}
      - input: ref('stg_shopflow_app__order_items')
        rows:
          - {order_item_id: 1, order_id: 1, quantity: 2, line_amount: 500.00}
          - {order_item_id: 2, order_id: 2, quantity: 1, line_amount: 80.00}
      # int_payments__per_order is EPHEMERAL (no relation in the database):
      # dbt cannot read its columns, so this input MUST use format: sql
      - input: ref('int_payments__per_order')
        format: sql
        rows: |
          select 1 as order_id, 1000.00 as amount_paid, 0.00 as amount_refunded
          union all
          select 2 as order_id, 80.00 as amount_paid, 80.00 as amount_refunded
      - input: ref('exchange_rates')
        rows:
          - {currency_code: MAD, rate_month: 2025-07-01, rate_to_eur: 0.0921}
          - {currency_code: MAD, rate_month: 2025-08-01, rate_to_eur: 0.0918}
          - {currency_code: USD, rate_month: 2025-12-01, rate_to_eur: 0.9168}
    expect:
      rows:
        - {order_id: 1, order_total: 500.00, net_amount: 1000.00, order_total_eur: 46.05, net_amount_eur: 92.10}
        - {order_id: 2, order_total: 80.00, net_amount: 0.00, order_total_eur: 73.34, net_amount_eur: 0.00}

with order_items as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__order_items') }}

),

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__orders') }}

),

products as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__products') }}

),

exchange_rates as (

    select * from {{ ref('exchange_rates') }}

)

select
    order_items.order_item_id,
    order_items.order_id,
    order_items.product_id,
    products.category,
    orders.order_date,
    orders.currency_code,
    order_items.quantity,
    order_items.unit_price,
    order_items.line_amount,
    exchange_rates.rate_to_eur,
    {{ convert_to_eur('order_items.line_amount', 'exchange_rates.rate_to_eur') }} as line_amount_eur
from order_items
inner join orders
    on order_items.order_id = orders.order_id
left join products
    on order_items.product_id = products.product_id
left join exchange_rates
    on  orders.currency_code = exchange_rates.currency_code
    and date_trunc('month', orders.order_date) = exchange_rates.rate_month
files.models/intermediate/int_orders__enriched:
with orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__orders') }}

),

items_per_order as (

    select
        order_id,
        count(*)         as number_of_lines,
        sum(quantity)    as number_of_units,
        sum(line_amount) as order_total
    from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__order_items') }}
    group by order_id

),

payments_per_order as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_payments__per_order') }}

),

exchange_rates as (

    select * from {{ ref('exchange_rates') }}

),

joined as (

    select
        orders.order_id,
        orders.customer_id,
        orders.order_at,
        orders.order_date,
        orders.order_status,
        orders.currency_code,
        orders.updated_at,
        coalesce(items_per_order.number_of_lines, 0)     as number_of_lines,
        coalesce(items_per_order.number_of_units, 0)     as number_of_units,
        coalesce(items_per_order.order_total, 0)         as order_total,
        coalesce(payments_per_order.amount_paid, 0)      as amount_paid,
        coalesce(payments_per_order.amount_refunded, 0)  as amount_refunded,
        exchange_rates.rate_to_eur
    from orders
    left join items_per_order
        on orders.order_id = items_per_order.order_id
    left join payments_per_order
        on orders.order_id = payments_per_order.order_id
    left join exchange_rates
        on  orders.currency_code = exchange_rates.currency_code
        and date_trunc('month', orders.order_date) = exchange_rates.rate_month

)

select
    *,
    amount_paid - amount_refunded                            as net_amount,
    {{ convert_to_eur('order_total') }}                      as order_total_eur,
    {{ convert_to_eur('amount_paid - amount_refunded') }}    as net_amount_eur
from joined
files.models/intermediate/int_payments__per_or:
{{ config(materialized='ephemeral') }}

with payments as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_payments_provider__payments') }}

),

refunds as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_payments_provider__refunds') }}

),

succeeded_payments as (

    -- money really received. The provider sent ONE negative row by mistake
    -- (payment 3170, found by the not_negative test in m06): we ignore it.
    select *
    from payments
    where payment_status = 'succeeded'
      and amount > 0

),

refunds_per_payment as (

    select
        payment_id,
        sum(amount) as refunded_amount
    from refunds
    group by payment_id

)

select
    succeeded_payments.order_id,
    count(*)                                          as number_of_payments,
    sum(succeeded_payments.amount)                    as amount_paid,
    coalesce(sum(refunds_per_payment.refunded_amount), 0) as amount_refunded,
    max(succeeded_payments.created_at)                as last_payment_at
from succeeded_payments
left join refunds_per_payment
    on succeeded_payments.payment_id = refunds_per_payment.payment_id
group by succeeded_payments.order_id

files.models/marts/finance/dim_products.sql:
with products as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__products') }}

),

latest_rates as (

    -- convert list prices with the most recent monthly rate
    select currency_code, rate_to_eur
    from {{ ref('exchange_rates') }}
    qualify rate_month = max(rate_month) over (partition by currency_code)

)

select
    products.product_id,
    products.sku,
    products.product_name,
    products.category,
    products.price,
    products.currency_code,
    {{ convert_to_eur('products.price', 'latest_rates.rate_to_eur') }} as price_eur,
    products.is_active,
    products.created_at,
    products.updated_at
from products
left join latest_rates
    on products.currency_code = latest_rates.currency_code
files.models/marts/finance/fct_daily_revenue.s:
{#- one row per day and sales region, days without orders included (revenue = 0) -#}

with days as (

    {{ dbt_utils.date_spine(
        datepart="day",
        start_date="cast('" ~ var('revenue_start_date') ~ "' as date)",
        end_date="cast('" ~ var('revenue_end_date') ~ "' as date)"
    ) }}

),

regions as (

    select distinct region from {{ ref('country_regions') }}

),

orders as (

    select
        orders.order_date,
        regions.region,
        orders.net_amount_eur
    from {{ ref('int_orders__enriched') }} as orders
    inner join {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__customers') }} as customers
        on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id
    inner join {{ ref('country_regions') }} as regions
        on customers.country_code = regions.country_code
    where orders.order_status <> 'cancelled'

),

daily as (

    select
        order_date,
        region,
        count(*)            as number_of_orders,
        sum(net_amount_eur) as revenue_eur
    from orders
    group by order_date, region

)

select
    {{ dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key(['days.date_day', 'regions.region']) }} as daily_revenue_key,
    cast(days.date_day as date)            as date_day,
    regions.region,
    coalesce(daily.number_of_orders, 0)    as number_of_orders,
    coalesce(daily.revenue_eur, 0)         as revenue_eur
from days
cross join regions
left join daily
    on  cast(days.date_day as date) = daily.order_date
    and regions.region = daily.region

files.models/marts/marketing/dim_customers.sql:
with customers as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_shopflow_app__customers') }}

),

regions as (

    select * from {{ ref('country_regions') }}

),

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_orders__enriched') }}
    where order_status <> 'cancelled'

),

customer_orders as (

    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_at)       as first_order_at,
        max(order_at)       as last_order_at,
        count(*)            as number_of_orders,
        sum(net_amount_eur) as lifetime_value_eur
    from orders
    group by customer_id

)

select
    customers.customer_id,
    customers.email,
    customers.first_name,
    customers.last_name,
    customers.country_code,
    regions.country_name,
    regions.region,
    customers.created_at,
    customer_orders.first_order_at,
    customer_orders.last_order_at,
    coalesce(customer_orders.number_of_orders, 0)   as number_of_orders,
    coalesce(customer_orders.lifetime_value_eur, 0) as lifetime_value_eur
from customers
left join regions
    on customers.country_code = regions.country_code
left join customer_orders
    on customers.customer_id = customer_orders.customer_id
files.models/marts/marketing/fct_sessions.sql:
{%- set event_types = ['page_view', 'add_to_cart', 'checkout_start', 'purchase'] -%}

with events as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_web_analytics__events') }}

)

select
    session_id,
    max(customer_id)                                  as customer_id,
    min(event_at)                                     as session_start_at,
    max(event_at)                                     as session_end_at,
    date_diff('second', min(event_at), max(event_at)) as session_duration_seconds,
    count(*)                                          as number_of_events,
    {%- for event_type in event_types %}
    count_if(event_type = '{{ event_type }}') as {{ event_type }}_events,
    {%- endfor %}
    count_if(event_type = 'purchase') > 0             as has_purchase,
    arg_min(page_path, event_at)                      as landing_page
from events
group by session_id
files.models/staging/payments_provider/_paymen:
models:
  - name: stg_payments_provider__payments
    description: One row per payment attempt. amount is in currency units (cents / 100).
    columns:
      - name: payment_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: order_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__orders')
                field: order_id
      - name: payment_status
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['succeeded', 'failed', 'pending']
      - name: payment_method
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['card', 'paypal', 'bank_transfer', 'cash_on_delivery', 'gift_card']
      - name: amount
        data_tests:
          - not_negative:
              config:
                severity: warn   # 1 wrong row from the provider; excluded in int_payments__per_order

  - name: stg_payments_provider__refunds
    description: One row per refund. refunded_at is a real timestamp.
    columns:
      - name: refund_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: payment_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_payments_provider__payments')
                field: payment_id
      - name: refunded_at
        data_tests: [not_null]

sources:
  - name: payments_provider
    description: Daily export of the payment provider. Amounts are integers in CENTS.
    schema: payments_provider
    tables:
      - name: payments
        description: One row per payment attempt (failed attempts included).
        columns:
          - name: payment_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
        config:
          loaded_at_field: _loaded_at
          freshness:
            warn_after: {count: 12, period: hour}
            error_after: {count: 24, period: hour}
      - name: refunds
        description: Money sent back to customers. refunded_at is TEXT (DD/MM/YYYY HH:MI).

files.models/staging/shopflow_app/_shopflow_ap:
models:
  - name: stg_shopflow_app__customers
    description: One row per customer (latest version), email cleaned (trim + lower case).
    data_tests:
      - dbt_utils.expression_is_true:
          arguments:
            expression: "email = lower(trim(email))"
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Primary key of a customer.
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: email
        description: Lower-case email without spaces. Can be NULL.
      - name: country_code
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('country_regions')
                field: country_code

  - name: stg_shopflow_app__addresses
    description: One row per address.
    columns:
      - name: address_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: customer_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__customers')
                field: customer_id
      - name: address_type
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['shipping', 'billing']

  - name: stg_shopflow_app__products
    description: One row per product. price is in currency_code (EUR, USD or MAD).
    columns:
      - name: product_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: sku
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: currency_code
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['EUR', 'USD', 'MAD']

  - name: stg_shopflow_app__orders
    description: One row per order with its current status.
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: customer_id
        data_tests:
          - not_null
          - relationships:
              name: orders_customer_exists
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__customers')
                field: customer_id
              config:
                # 1 known orphan order (customer 9999, ticket APP-412): warn, but fail if it grows
                warn_if: ">0"
                error_if: ">10"
                store_failures: true
      - name: order_status
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['pending', 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'returned']
      - name: currency_code
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['EUR', 'USD', 'MAD']

  - name: stg_shopflow_app__order_items
    description: One row per order line. Amounts are in the order currency.
    columns:
      - name: order_item_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: order_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__orders')
                field: order_id
      - name: product_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__products')
                field: product_id
      - name: quantity
        data_tests:
          - dbt_utils.accepted_range:
              arguments:
                min_value: 1

sources:
  - name: shopflow_app
    description: Copy of the ShopFlow application database, loaded every night by the EL tool.
    schema: shopflow_app
    tables:
      - name: customers
        description: One row per customer account (the export can contain an old copy of a row).
        columns:
          - name: customer_id
            data_tests:
              - not_null
              - unique:
                  config:
                    severity: warn   # known: old copies of rows; removed in staging
      - name: addresses
        description: Shipping and billing addresses of the customers.
      - name: products
        description: Product catalogue. Prices are in the currency of the listing (EUR, USD or MAD).
      - name: orders
        description: One row per order, with its current status.
        columns:
          - name: order_id
            data_tests: [unique, not_null]
        config:
          loaded_at_field: _loaded_at
          freshness:
            warn_after: {count: 12, period: hour}
            error_after: {count: 24, period: hour}
      - name: order_items
        description: One row per product line of an order. unit_price is in the order currency.

files.models/staging/web_analytics/_web_analyt:
models:
  - name: stg_web_analytics__events
    description: One row per tracked event, duplicates removed.
    columns:
      - name: event_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: event_type
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: ['page_view', 'add_to_cart', 'checkout_start', 'purchase']
      - name: customer_id
        description: NULL for visitors who are not logged in (relationships ignores NULLs).
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('stg_shopflow_app__customers')
                field: customer_id

sources:
  - name: web_analytics
    description: Events sent by the website tracker (installed on 2025-10-01).
    schema: web_analytics
    config:
      loaded_at_field: _loaded_at
      freshness:
        warn_after: {count: 6, period: hour}
        error_after: {count: 24, period: hour}
    tables:
      - name: events
        description: One row per tracked event. The tracker sometimes sends an event twice.
        columns:
          - name: event_id
            data_tests:
              - not_null
              - unique:
                  config:
                    severity: warn   # known: the tracker re-sends events; removed in staging

unit_tests:
  - name: test_duplicate_events_keep_the_first_copy
    description: When the tracker sends the same event_id twice, staging keeps the copy loaded first.
    model: stg_web_analytics__events
    given:
      - input: source('web_analytics', 'events')
        format: csv
        rows: |
          event_id,session_id,customer_id,event_type,event_timestamp,page,_loaded_at
          e1,s1,,page_view,2025-12-01 10:00:00,/,2025-12-01 10:20:00
          e1,s1,,page_view,2025-12-01 10:00:00,/,2025-12-01 10:35:00
          e2,s1,,add_to_cart,2025-12-01 10:02:00,/cart,2025-12-01 10:21:00
    expect:
      format: csv
      rows: |
        event_id,event_type,loaded_at
        e1,page_view,2025-12-01 10:20:00
        e2,add_to_cart,2025-12-01 10:21:00

seeds:
  - name: exchange_rates
    description: >
      Monthly exchange rates used by finance. 1 unit of currency_code = rate_to_eur EUR.
      One row per currency and month (first day of the month).
    config:
      column_types:
        currency_code: varchar
        rate_month: date
        rate_to_eur: decimal(12, 6)
    columns:
      - name: currency_code
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: rate_month
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: rate_to_eur
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: country_regions
    description: Country code -> country name, sales region and default currency.
    config:
      column_types:
        country_code: varchar
        country_name: varchar
        region: varchar
        default_currency: varchar
    columns:
      - name: country_code
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]

files.snapshots/snapshots.yml:
snapshots:
  - name: products_snapshot
    description: >
      History of the product catalogue (price, active flag). The app keeps a reliable
      updated_at column, so we use the timestamp strategy.
    relation: source('shopflow_app', 'products')
    config:
      schema: snapshots
      unique_key: product_id
      strategy: timestamp
      updated_at: updated_at

  - name: shipments_snapshot
    description: >
      History of shipment statuses. We only want a new version when the status or the
      delivery time changes (not when the loader touches the row), so we use the check strategy.
    relation: source('shipping', 'shipments')
    config:
      schema: snapshots
      unique_key: shipment_id
      strategy: check
      check_cols: ['status', 'delivered_at']
-- Singular test: an order that was paid must have received exactly its total.
-- Returns the orders where this is not true (0 rows = PASS).
select
    order_id,
    order_status,
    order_total,
    amount_paid
from {{ ref('fct_orders') }}
where order_status in ('paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'returned')
  and amount_paid <> order_total
-- Singular test: we can never refund more than what the customer paid.
select
    order_id,
    amount_paid,
    amount_refunded
from {{ ref('fct_orders') }}
where amount_refunded > amount_paid
